comparator.name: Bachelor Industrial Engineering
comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 current programme and course records; official 180-EC curriculum checked 2026-10-05
comparator.sourceNotes: The current TU/e programme material and accreditation report establish a broad 180-EC Industrial Engineering bachelor organised around mathematics, industrial engineering and integration of engineering with business. The official curriculum accounts for three 60-EC years and includes calculus, statistics, business economics, financial management, social and organisational psychology, information systems, programming, operations research, operations planning and control, accounting, quality and reliability, business-system design, simulation, project management, 45 EC of elective space and a 10-EC company-based Bachelor End Project. Current 2026-2027 course records substantiate statistics, operations planning and control and supply-chain content. No formal bachelor route is selected.

candidates.reason: UCR can address economics, sustainability, organisational decisions and data analysis, but the catalogue has no supply-chain-management, logistics, procurement, inventory-control, production-planning or transport-operations sequence. A separate 24-course route would replace the evidenced supply-chain direction with general sustainability and business study.

selection.assessment: The closest programme combines business, economics, organisations, data, programming, optimisation and information systems while clearly displaying UCR's lack of a dedicated operations-management spine. A second coherent route gives digital business systems, AI and technological innovation a materially different curricular priority. The remaining sustainable-supply-chain direction cannot be implemented as a credible 24-course programme from the available catalogue.

alternatives.label: Industrial decisions, data & organisational systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines business and economics with statistics, data, programming, optimisation, information systems, organisations, product design, communication and empirical decision-making.
alternatives.concept: The closest UCR response combines business economics, finance, organisational psychology, information systems, programming, data, statistics, optimisation, product design and research. It supports evidence-based process and organisational decisions while preserving TU/e's dedicated operations research, production planning, logistics, quality-engineering and repeated industrial projects as material limitations.
progression: Business, programming, data, mathematics and research foundations precede machine learning, organisational psychology, digital transformation, optimisation, algorithms, governance, econometrics, market research, negotiation and probability. Formal prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Digital business systems, AI & innovation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum gives greater weight to programming, networks, databases, algorithms, machine learning, neural networks, AI decision-making and ethics, connected to organisational strategy and innovation.
alternatives.concept: This distinct route focuses on digital information systems, AI and technological innovation in organisations. It combines programming, databases, networks, algorithms, machine learning, neural networks, optimisation and AI ethics with entrepreneurship, organisational psychology, strategy, governance, market research and communication.
progression: Programming, data, mathematics, business and research foundations precede networks, databases, machine learning, AI decision-making, optimisation, business uses of AI, algorithms, organisational psychology, deep learning and advanced market research. Formal prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces leadership communication, accounting and finance, behavioural economics, econometrics and negotiation with AI ethics, networks and operating systems, AI decision-making, business uses of AI and neural networks. Each route has five courses, or 37.5 EC, not present in the other.

blocks: Mathematical Methods includes calculus and quantitative modelling.
Research Methods & Statistics covers probability, inference and empirical research design.
Probability & Statistics supports stochastic analysis, while TU/e provides dedicated stochastic operations research.
Introduction to Data Science supports data analysis, while TU/e's course centres discrete-event simulation of operations.
Optimization Methods in AI directly addresses search, optimisation and constraints, but not the full operations-research sequence.
Introduction to Programming provides the computational foundation.
Database Management Systems directly addresses information storage and organisational data systems.
AI Ethics addresses societal and ethical consequences of digital business systems.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations introduces business models and problem framing, but not the full industrial-engineering field.
Introduction to Economics provides firm and market foundations.
Accounting & Corporate Finance directly covers accounting and financial analysis.
Microeconomics & Behavior supports firm and investment decisions, while TU/e provides dedicated financial management.
Consumer Product Design directly addresses product-development processes, customer needs and prototyping.
UCR offers accounting, finance and economics but no separate advanced financial-management course.
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership directly covers organisational behaviour, culture, teams and change.
Persuasive Communication covers social influence and behavioural change; TU/e provides a broader social-psychology foundation.
Operations, process design and industrial projects
UCR has optimisation and business-process analysis but no dedicated operations-planning and control course.
UCR has no equivalent applied operations-planning project.
UCR has no equivalent operations-management simulation game.
UCR distributes system and organisational design across courses but has no equivalent integrated industrial project.
UCR has no equivalent advanced business-system design project.
UCR has no dedicated quality and reliability engineering course.
Project work appears across UCR courses, but project management is not offered as a dedicated course.
TU/e preserves 5 EC of first-year elective space; the UCR pathways are complete fixed examples.
TU/e preserves 20 EC of second-year elective space.
TU/e preserves 30 EC of third-year elective space.
TU/e requires a 10-EC individual company-based Bachelor End Project. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes combine business, organisations, quantitative methods, data and information systems. TU/e additionally provides a dedicated cumulative sequence in operations research, production and inventory planning, logistics, quality and reliability engineering, operations simulation, repeated industrial design projects and a compulsory company-based Bachelor End Project. Those specialist operations components are not offered at UCR.
